title: Couple a delivery hose to a tank outlet with a camlock fitting: seat the coupler, then close both cam arms
instruction: Couple the hose to the tank outlet: seat the coupler fully on the adapter, then close both cam arms.
context: Coupling a delivery hose to a tank outlet with a camlock fitting is a core operation for tanker drivers among heavy and tractor-trailer truck drivers (about 2.0 million US workers, BLS OEWS May 2023). The difficulty is physical: the coupler's bore leaves 6 mm of play around the adapter and must be lowered straight over it until it seats on the collar, then its two cam arms are pushed down from just above horizontal through a 100-degree arc, one gripper on each side. Closed arms hang below the coupler, so an arm closed before seating stops the coupler going on.
setup: Positions are measured on the table from the point midway between the two arm bases, which stand 61 cm apart: forward means away from the arms, left and right as seen from behind the arms. Tank outlet (tank_outlet, fixed): an aluminium male camlock adapter, 36 mm across and 5.7 cm tall with a collar 3 cm up, on a steel base plate 27 cm forward on the centre line. Dummy adapter (dummy_adapter, fixed): the same at 15 cm forward, 24 cm right. Coupler (coupler, 250 g): the hose's female camlock coupler, an aluminium sleeve 6 cm square outside with a 48 mm bore, 3 cm tall, a capped top with a black 30 mm hose stub 4 cm tall, and two yellow cam arms (arm_left, arm_right joints) 5.5 cm long hinged at the sleeve's top on its left and right sides; it starts seated on the dummy adapter with both arms open, 10 degrees above horizontal (hinge friction 0.03 N m). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The coupler is seated when its axis is within 4 mm of the tank adapter's (seen from above), it rests on the collar (within 4 mm of seated height) and stands upright (within 5 degrees). An arm is closed when it hangs within 8 degrees of straight down. Score at the end of the trial: 0.3 for the coupler seated and still, plus 0.15 per arm closed while it is seated (0 to 0.6). 1.0 when the coupler is seated with both arms closed, nothing moves and no gripper tool point is within 4 cm of the hose stub or an arm, held for 1 s (the trial then ends; completed less than 1 s before the run limit scores 0.6). 0 if the coupler falls off the table.
reset_notes: Put the coupler back on its dummy adapter with both cam arms raised open.
fidelity: Approximate. The camlock's cams, groove and gasket are not modelled: the arms are friction-held hinged levers and coupling is judged by seating and arm angle. Square-section sleeve walls stand in for the round sleeve; no hose is attached to the stub. PhysX rigid-body contacts with default friction.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (coupler never seated on the tank adapter; one cam arm knocked shut on the parked coupler; hit the 120 s step limit); demo: 1.0 (coupler carried onto the tank adapter and seated on its collar, both cam arms pushed down closed, hands clear, held 1 s)
